pages.text: After adding a station to a timetable, click it again with the same timetable to say what the train does with wagons there. Each click goes on to the next:$(li)$(l)Leave$() a wagon, or 2, 3 or 4, or all of them$(li)$(l)Pick up$() waiting wagons$(li)Nothing to do with wagons$(br)The tooltip shows what each stop does.

Leaving, it uncouples cars from the end it won't be leading with when it sets off again, and leaves them standing. Coming back out of a dead-end siding it leaves the ones at the far end, so push them in with the engine at the back.$(br2)Picking up, it runs up to wagons standing near the nameboard, couples on, and takes them along.
The diesel's left two wagons at the goods yard.

For example: a goods train running Quarry, then Yard (leave 2 wagons) leaves two wagons at the yard every trip; a second engine running Yard (pick up), then Works (leave all) brings them on to the works.$(br2)Leave wagons on level track: loose wagons roll on a slope (a guard's van's handbrake holds them).
